discussion.text:
000
FXUS63 KIWX 060816
AFDIWX

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Northern Indiana
316 AM EST Fri Nov 6 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Scattered to numerous lake effect rain showers today into
  tonight, mainly for areas west of Interstate 69 in northern IN
  and southwest MI.

- Cool and breezy today into Saturday with highs near 50 degrees.

- Dry and warmer than average weather returns early next week.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 316 AM EST Fri Nov 6 2026

Areas of light rain and drizzle associated with a positively 
tilted upper trough and cold front should exit eastern zones by
12z. Today into tonight then features a transition to lake 
enhanced/effect rain showers thanks to ongoing cold advection 
within deepening north-northwest flow. This occurs on the 
backside of a potent vort lobe dropping southeast through the 
central/eastern Great Lakes. More intense banding may set up for
a time in sw MI and nc IN later this morning through this 
evening as the prevailing flow becomes parallel to the long axis
of Lake MI resulting in stronger frictional/thermal convergence
over eastern Lake MI. Localized rainfall amounts may exceed a 
half inch in spots, best chances Berrien MI down into 
LaPorte/South Bend/Plymouth. Drying and subsidence eventually 
takes its toll on inversion heights by later tonight and 
Saturday bringing an end to more organized LE rain. Cooler and 
somewhat breezy early November wx otherwise today into Saturday.

Flow regime flattens out Sunday into early next week with more 
active westerlies shifting off to the north-northeast. Return west-
southwest flow will usher in a milder pacific air mass with 
sunshine and warm advection resulting in a return to above 
normal temps. Some degree of upper troughing and CAA then
settles back in for the second half of next week with near 
normal temps and non-zero rain shower chances. 

&&

.AVIATION /06Z TAFS THROUGH 06Z SATURDAY/...
Issued at 1253 AM EST Fri Nov 6 2026

Areas of drizzle and light rain showers with MVFR CIGS and VSBYs
within the drizzle associated with a cold front currently 
draped northeast to southwest over the middle of the forecast 
area will continue to push southeastward. Drier air will usher 
in behind the front, at least for areas not downwind of Lake 
Michigan with a northerly flow introducing lake effect light 
rain showers to these locales. Kept light rain showers mentioned
for KSBN through 18z Fri and KFWA showers/drizzle should come 
to an end after 08z Fri or so. Northerly winds will veer to more
northwesterly late in the period with gusts of 20 to 25 kts
possible.

&&

.IWX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
IN...None.
OH...None.
MI...None.
MARINE...Small Craft Advisory until 4 PM EST Saturday for LMZ043-046.

&&

$$

DISCUSSION...Steinwedel
AVIATION...Andersen

spc.text:
SPC AC 060553

   Day 1 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1153 PM CST Thu Nov 05 2026

   Valid 061200Z - 071200Z

   ...THERE IS A MARGINAL RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS FROM PORTIONS OF
   THE CAROLINAS TO THE MID ATLANTIC COAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Isolated strong to severe storms are possible over parts of the
   eastern Carolinas and southern Mid Atlantic Coast.

   ...Carolinas/Atlantic Coast...
   An upper low over eastern Great Lakes at the start of the forecast
   period is forecast merge with a shortwave trough moving from the mid
   MS Valley across the central Appalachians. A belt of enhanced
   deep-layer southwesterly flow will accompany the low across much of
   the Eastern Seaboard. At the surface, a cold front and broad area of
   low pressure will stretch from southern New England to eastern North
   Carolina. The low and front should gradually strengthen as they and
   the upper trough move offshore into early Saturday morning.

   Early in the period ahead of the cold front, a band of scattered
   showers and thunderstorms are likely to be ongoing from southern New
   England to the Carolinas, associated with continued northward
   advection of mid 60s to low 70s F surface dewpoints. Enhanced flow
   aloft will overspread the area through the morning generally
   parallel to the advancing front. The strongest upper-level winds
   will likely remain on the cool side of the boundary, but model
   soundings show effective shear values increasing to 30-40 kt within
   the warm sector by late morning.

   Given the presence of the unseasonably humid air mass, diurnal
   heating and destabilization will tend to be muted by residual cloud
   cover, especially with northward extent. Still, cooling mid-level
   temperatures and modest buoyancy (MLCAPE ~500 J/kg) should be
   sufficient to maintain isolated stronger storms eastward through
   midday. Some organization into linear clusters or short bowing
   segments is possible which would support a risk for damaging gusts.
   Adequate hodograph curvature in the lowest 1-2 km could also support
   a brief tornado before convection weakens and moves offshore later
   in the afternoon/early evening.

   ...AZ...
   A second upper trough will move from the southern Great Basin into
   the Southwest today and tonight. Cold mid-level temperatures will
   accompany the upper trough, steeping mid-level lapse rates and
   allowing for weak elevated buoyancy to develop. However the limited
   instability and vertical shear should preclude a severe risk outside
   of sporadic hail with an isolated stronger storm.

   ..Lyons/Halbert-K.. 11/06/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS01 PTSDY1 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 1 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 1300Z

spc.text:
SPC AC 060654

   Day 2 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1254 AM CST Fri Nov 06 2026

   Valid 071200Z - 081200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Severe thunderstorms are not forecast across the U.S. Saturday and
   Saturday night.

   ...DISCUSSION...
   An upper-level low and an associated trough will move eastward
   across the Northeast on Saturday, reaching the western Atlantic
   Saturday night. Another upper-level low will move slowly across
   northern Mexico. In response to this second system, low-level
   moisture will return northward into southern and central Texas
   Saturday and Saturday night. As lift gradually increases due to the
   approach of the system, scattered thunderstorms will be possible
   from parts of south and central Texas westward into the Trans-Pecos
   from Saturday afternoon into the overnight period. Instability is
   expected to be too weak for a severe threat. Elsewhere across the
   continental U.S., thunderstorms are not forecast Saturday or
   Saturday night.

   ..Broyles.. 11/06/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS02 PTSDY2 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 2 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 1730Z

spc.text:
SPC AC 060724

   Day 3 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   0124 AM CST Fri Nov 06 2026

   Valid 081200Z - 091200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   No severe threat is forecast across the continental U.S. Sunday and
   Sunday night.

   ...DISCUSSION...
   Northwest flow at mid-levels is expected on Sunday from the
   north-central states to the Eastern Seaboard. Further southwest, an
   upper-level low is forecast to move toward the Rio Grande Valley of
   southwest Texas. A moist airmass will likely be located over south
   and central Texas, where scattered to numerous thunderstorms will be
   possible during the day. Thunderstorms may continue across parts of
   south Texas in the overnight period. Instability is forecast to be
   weak across south and central Texas, making severe thunderstorm
   development unlikely. Elsewhere across the continental U.S.,
   thunderstorms are not expected Sunday and Sunday night.

   ..Broyles.. 11/06/2026

consensus.about: NWS next to four computer models (Open-Meteo, CC BY 4.0). blend = the middle value of NWS and the models; adjusted = blend corrected by our own average past error at the La Porte airport once 14+ days are graded (capped at 3 degrees). Rain chances are NWS's. suggested = what the Daily Scoop's forecasts use (tomorrow and the day after).

bias.note: Average of (forecast minus airport reading) over the last 30 graded days; positive means we ran warm. Used to nudge the model blend once 14+ days are graded.
